newsitem.title: GERMANY: Blackmailers spike mustard with cyanide in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Blackmailers spike mustard with cyanide in Germany.

text.p: Police probing an attempt to blackmail a German food manufacturer said on Tuesday they had discovered two tubes of mustard laced with cyanide in two separate German supermarkets.

Police said they had discovered the mustard in stores in Saarbruecken in the southwest and Regensburg in the southeast, planted to force mustard manufacturer Thomy, a unit of Switzerland's Nestle, to pay a large sum of money.

Frankfurt police, who are coordinating the investigation, said the supermarkets where the finds were made, along with another in the northern town of Bremen, had been closed after extortionists sent a new threatening letter.

Thomy has been receiving letters threatening to contaminate its products for several months. The company said it had received an "ominous" letter on Monday, which warned: "This time it's not just Thomy products."
Police appealed to the public not to consume any products bought in the three supermarkets in the first week of April and to return purchases to the stores in return for a refund.

German police last month arrested a couple suspected of blackmailing Nestle's Maggi subsidiary by threatening to infect its products with mad cow disease unless it handed over one million marks ($580,000).
